note: Release notes shown in Settings → Advanced → Version. Newest first. SHORT, PLAIN bullets under "features" and "fixes" — a line or two each, no jargon, no filler; anyone who wants the long story can read the repo. Every release needs at least one bullet. Set "critical": true on a release that fixes data loss, a security issue, or a breaking sync change so the desktop calls it out.

entries.headline: Apps open straight into their room, with sound
features: Opening an app link now goes straight into the app with a small audio bar: who is here, mute, leave, and a Full meeting button for cameras and the Stage.
Meetings and broadcasts each have their own lighter page, so they load less.
fixes: Every old meeting and broadcast link still opens the same room.

entries.headline: Everyone in a meeting now runs the same GifOS
features: Older GifOS pages are asked to update before they join, so a meeting never mixes versions and a hosted meeting's size always comes from its permissions.
fixes: The License dialog's Close button now looks like the other dialogs' buttons.
The embedded player shares its video controls and Stage blur reading with the meeting page.

entries.headline: Meeting size is now kept by the meeting service, from the permissions shown in the room
features: Hosted meetings: anyone in the room can open More → License to see the permissions the meeting holds, such as "Up to 20 people" or "No people limit".
A permission someone brings stays with the meeting for as long as it runs, even after they leave.
fixes: A full hosted meeting now says so at once, with the number of people it holds, and lets you in by itself when a place opens.

entries.headline: Embedded broadcasts show LIVE at once; the Stage is blurred the same everywhere
features: Settings → Floating window shows is a clearer list with bigger Move up / Move down buttons, now in every language.
Plans and help now say it plainly: video gets through company and school firewalls, still end-to-end encrypted.
fixes: gifos.app/welcome and other embeds opened after the host arrived now show LIVE in seconds instead of "not hosted" for up to two minutes.
The Stage picture of a camera-off person is blurred the same on /meet, /cast and embeds, following the room's blur rules.
After a short network drop on a firewalled network, the relay link comes back in seconds instead of leaving you alone for half a minute or more.

entries.headline: Use your plan on more devices; restore it if you lose them
features: Use your plan on another device: scan a code on gifos.app/subscription.
Lost your device? Restore your plan by signing in with PayPal.
gifos.app/subscription now manages everything about your plan, with full receipts.
fixes: Plan checks refuse a class of weak keys that no real device makes.
The share-screen sheet now says the truth: your camera stays on and everyone sees your screen on the Stage.

entries.headline: Choose what the floating window shows; embed a live broadcast
features: Settings has a "Floating window shows" list: put an app, a shared screen or the Stage first, then follow the speaker.
Put a live GifOS broadcast in any web page with gifos.app/embed. gifos.app/welcome shows how.
Apps can list their own tips and purchases on this device.
fixes: The floating window follows whoever is talking, camera off or in the Stadium, instead of sticking to the Stadium picture.

entries.headline: Talking frames on shared screens and the Stage
fixes: The green talking frame now lights for someone sharing a screen or on the Stage.
A person with the camera off shows their letter, not a black square, in a packed row.

entries.headline: Bots can speak right away
fixes: A bot in your meeting is heard from its first spoken line.

entries.headline: Blurred pictures stay blurred when floated
fixes: A picture you see blurred now stays blurred in picture-in-picture, too.

entries.headline: Private room links
features: Copied and shared meeting links now keep the room name after a #, so it is never sent to any server. Old links still open the same rooms.

entries.headline: Blur holds everywhere you watch
fixes: Blurred video now stays blurred in row and stadium views, the Stage strip, picture-in-picture and Stage views.

entries.headline: Clearer payments and receipts
features: Paying with USDC now says up front that your wallet asks for two approvals: the GifOS fee first, then the creator.
Receipts open in their own receipt view, with a link to check each payment on the blockchain explorer, or to your PayPal activity.
Your GifOS Meet subscriptions are kept as receipts in Purchases.
fixes: Broadcast: no extra red band under the top banner, and the on-air chip shows one dot.
Terms: updated content rules and the plan meeting count.

entries.headline: Tidier meeting code underneath
fixes: The meeting page's screen code now reads the meeting through one small table. Nothing you see or hear changes.

entries.headline: Plans read the same everywhere, and disconnect your wallet
features: Settings shows the wallet you connected and a Disconnect wallet button. The pay sheet has Use a different wallet.
fixes: Your plan or pass now gives the same rights in meetings, storage, TURN and bots, read from what you bought, not the plan's name.
The Plans page marks what your pass already includes.

entries.headline: Sound on older iPhones and iPads, and muted listeners float
features: Muted? If you allowed the microphone before, hiding the meeting tab now floats it in a small window too. Your mic stays muted: nobody hears you until you tap Mic. The browser shows the microphone as in use while you are in the meeting.
fixes: Older iPhones and iPads that played no meeting sound now hear everyone.
Game seats belong to the meeting you are in: players in another meeting no longer hold your seats.
Joining through a strict firewall connects about 6 seconds sooner when the other side starts the link.

entries.headline: No more getting stuck knocking at the door
fixes: Coming back to a meeting while another of your devices sleeps (say, an iPad left open) no longer leaves you knocking: you get in within seconds.
The host gets straight into their own meeting, even when they arrive after a guest.
A meeting with no host present lets people in at once, up to the free size, instead of waiting for the host's plan.

entries.headline: You hear the people beside you as soon as you sit down
features: When you join, you hear the people in your row as soon as you are seated, about two seconds sooner than before.
fixes: Store links open the store page directly, and the Update bar and home screen store icon take you there.
A new version of GifOS takes over without reloading your open pages, and the subscription page's words work offline.
A browser too old to run meetings (Firefox before 78, Chrome before 73) now says so clearly instead of hanging on "Joining…".

entries.headline: A clear green frame on whoever is talking
features: Whoever is talking now gets a clear green frame on their tile, the other people in the meeting included, not just your own tile.
fixes: iPhone and iPad: when Safari holds the meeting's sound, the "tap to hear" line stays until sound really plays, and one tap brings it back.
More now says "Sound plays from this device's speaker" when there is no speaker to choose.

entries.headline: App signing keys can live in DNS
features: App signing: a domain can now publish its signing key as a DNS TXT record (_gifos.yourdomain) instead of, or as well as, the gifos.key file — handy when you can't set web server headers.
fixes: Smoother German, Russian and Chinese wording on the captions language card and caption choices.

entries.headline: Meeting, Broadcast and the App Store open straight from the Home Screen
fixes: On a first visit, tapping Meeting on the Home Screen could say "This app isn't on this device". Meeting, Broadcast and the App Store now open their page directly.
The Terms and Privacy pages list every plan, and Broadcast points to the Meet terms and privacy policy.

entries.headline: New plans for running several meetings at once, and a Plans page
features: Plans for several meetings at once: Family business, 5 meetings ($19.90 a month or $199 a year); Small business, 10 ($34.90 a month or $349 a year); Business, 100 ($2,999 a year); Large business, 1,000 ($24,999 a year); Enterprise, 10,000 ($199,000 a year, billed monthly). For more, write to support@gifos.app.
A new Plans page (gifos.app/subscription) lists every plan, marks the one you have, and shows the way up.
Moving up to a bigger plan gives you credit for the time left, so its first charge is smaller; later charges are the full price.
Plans and passes you hold add up: each one covers its own number of meetings at once.
When every meeting your plan covers is in use, GifOS asks before moving it to a new one. Organization plans never take a place from another meeting: the new one runs on the free limits.
fixes: The Terms describe the new plans.

entries.headline: You keep your seat when a laptop in the meeting goes to sleep
fixes: In a meeting of two, the person who stays keeps their seat while the other's laptop sleeps.
A person whose laptop slept comes back to their own seat, and whoever stood in for them steps back instead of being sent out.
A seat that already sat elsewhere no longer holds up the line at a second door.
Two offices joined over a relay link rejoin their meeting when their own link breaks.

entries.headline: Sound recovers faster when someone passing it along goes quiet
fixes: Sound recovers faster when someone passing it along to your part of a big meeting goes quiet.

entries.headline: Under the hood: more groundwork for lighter meeting bots
fixes: Under the hood: more groundwork for lighter meeting bots.

entries.headline: Under the hood: groundwork for lighter meeting bots
features: Under the hood: groundwork for lighter meeting bots.

entries.headline: Guests on hotel and venue Wi-Fi join faster
fixes: Meetings: Guests on hotel and venue Wi-Fi join much faster.
Meetings: Sound between linked offices no longer drops one way.

entries.headline: Live captions work in Microsoft Edge
fixes: Meetings: Live captions now work in Microsoft Edge. Edge listens to your meeting microphone, the same one everyone hears.

entries.headline: Follow the speaker keeps up
fixes: Meetings: Follow the speaker now moves to a new talker even when your page is busy, and a short pause still ends a turn so the view moves on.

entries.headline: A faster, cleaner meeting page, and more multiplayer apps
features: Meetings: the meeting page is rebuilt on one shared engine, so it loads lighter and behaves the same everywhere; nothing changes in how you use it.
Apps: more store apps now know who is in the meeting and hand hosting on when someone leaves, among them Hextris, Mermaid, Paint Board, HexGL, Memory and Floppy Bird.

entries.headline: Captions you can steer, and recordings that are never empty
features: Captions: picking a language teaches the automatic setting a starting point, never a lock, and the card says what moved.
Captions: the Captions button is now on Stage and in the stadium.
fixes: Recordings no longer come out empty when nobody in the meeting has a mic on.

entries.headline: Captions that adapt, and turns that skip empty seats
features: Captions: when others hear a different language than your captions, your page suggests switching, and only your tap changes it.
Captions: one card for a person's captions, with an example and a Captions button on their tile; the cards sit above the floating bar.
Apps: in turn-based games the turn skips empty seats and passes to the next person who is seated.
Apps: the party games and spy, dial and roulette have a choice of playing together or on one phone.
AI agents: an agent on stage follows the same rules as a person: it asks to speak, or raises a hand in a hosted room.
fixes: Captions: no silent restart in a learned language; a detected language only offers the suggestion.
Apps: Connect Four and other two-player games let the second person move after the host.

entries.headline: Rooms that fill fairly, and apps that know who is here
features: Apps: Take Turns, Guestbook, Chat, Bible Browser, Tic-Tac-Toe, Chess Tournament and the party games take the people from the meeting itself, so the list of who is here is always right and nobody who left lingers.
Apps: the party games (Odd Word Out, Catch the Spy, The Dial, Party Roulette) take their players from the meeting. Passing one phone around lives on in separate Single Phone versions.
AI agents: the guide for agents names the agent library and explains how an agent stays in a meeting.
fixes: Meetings: in a hosted room with a people limit, the limit holds even when many people join at once, and a seat promised to someone is not given to someone else.
Meetings: a hosted room with a people limit lets people in as fast as a room without one.
Meetings: when the person who links a row of seats stalls, the people behind them keep hearing the room, and hear everyone again as soon as that person is back.
Meetings: a page still on 0.9.27.1 or older updates at once when it joins a meeting, so everyone in a room runs the same version.
Phone apps: white chess pieces show properly, mic clips play in full, and the ... menu is easier to read.
Tic-Tac-Toe and Chess: a note that a move was refused stays until you tap or the room changes.

entries.headline: Agents you can hear, and full rooms that stay one
features: AI agents: an agent's voice is heard from its very first sentence, even before it sends any video.
AI agents: an agent can open an App Store app by its store id.
Meetings: a page that falls behind the GifOS its meeting runs on says so plainly, in a clearer bar with an Update now button.
fixes: Meetings: a full room no longer splits newcomers off into a second room. They wait a moment and knock again politely until there is space.
Meetings: the host's AI note takers setting now reaches every page in the meeting, not only the host's.
Meetings: stage audio stays steady when two people change what they send at the same moment.
Meetings: a meeting linked between offices is kept while people are still in it, so a computer that paused can find its way back.
Plans: an older pass saved in your browser no longer stops a new pass from being added.

entries.headline: Agents join in, and meetings hold steadier
features: AI agents: a page made for agents. An agent can join a meeting, follow what is said, speak, chat, raise a hand, watch and send video, and use the stage and apps, through one simple page and a small Node library.
AI agents: an agent page shows a plain text view built for machines, with one tap back to the normal view.
Meetings: hosts can choose whether AI note takers are allowed, need to ask, or are off. Anyone can hide bots from their own view.
Plans: every plan and pass now carries exactly what it allows, signed, so the door checks the same thing everywhere.
fixes: Meetings: a page left open on an older GifOS moves itself to this release when it joins a meeting, so everyone in a meeting runs the same version.
Meetings: open-floor rooms keep their agenda, stage and renames fair for everyone, and someone voted out stays out once the password changes.
Meetings: after a network change or a long pause, a page finds its way back into its meeting by itself.
Meetings: links between offices use less data when nobody is talking, so free links stay within their limit.
Meetings: a guest on a network that keeps devices apart starts its meeting as soon as it knows it cannot reach the others directly.
Meetings: when a link between rooms goes away, the people who need it get a new one instead of waiting.
Apps: Connect Four tells a player on an older GifOS that they need to update, in plain words.

entries.headline: Meetings that come together
features: Meetings: people who join the same meeting from different offices or networks now come together into one meeting much faster.
Meetings: the People list shows everyone by name, even people far away in a big meeting or in another office, and shows whether they are muted, have their camera off or have a hand up.
Meetings: a browser that cannot make calls of its own can still join. Someone already in the meeting carries its sound and chat.
Apps: games like Connect Four now play together with everyone in the meeting. GifOS keeps the seats, the turns and the line of people waiting to play.
Apps: Survey sits with Take Turns. Ask the room, and everyone sees the counts.
Meetings: any room name works, even a short word like "1" or "test".
Meetings: the AI assistant switch is in the lobby, before you join.
Meetings: every item in the More menu has its own icon.
Meetings: when a meeting is full, the door says how full it is and offers a way in: a $1 pass for 4 hours, or a plan. After you buy, you are let in without reloading.
fixes: Meetings: when someone on the link between two offices leaves, the offices hear each other again within about 5 seconds instead of up to 20.
Meetings: joining stays fast for real people, while floods of automated joiners slow down, and it is harder for anyone to grab a meeting unfairly.
Meetings: captions ignore garbled text from a broken or tampered sender.
Meetings: tapping Mic opens only the microphone, asks which one when you have more than one, and keeps the captions notice on screen.

entries.headline: Survey is in the meeting
features: Survey sits with Take Turns. Ask the room, and everyone sees the counts.
Run an app keeps its choices on a short window.

entries.headline: Assistant mode turns on or off
features: Assistant mode turns on or off. The switch shows which.

entries.headline: A tap starts the sound
features: A tap starts the sound, and the notice stays up until you can hear it.

entries.headline: Agenda, assistants, and a quieter join
features: The lobby choices are tabs, and Go live uses the room password alone.
An agenda item shows its length and stops at 120 characters. Alt+J opens the agenda.
A link for AI assistants is on the meeting and the lobby. One tap turns assistant mode on.
Joining with the camera and microphone off asks for neither.
Debug logging starts when you turn it on.
The meeting tab shows its icon.
Choosing No blur shows a clear preview. A meeting that keeps the picture blurred explains why.

entries.headline: A clearer way to start
features: Join, host, or open an open-floor meeting from one button.
The room password stays on the form when you host and when you go live.

entries.headline: Bring your AI assistant
features: Connect your AI assistant to GifOS from more places.
An assistant can join a meeting in its own browser, choose its name, and take part in the chat.

entries.headline: More reliable joining
fixes: Joining is more reliable when someone joins from a phone.
Meetings always connect, even if a saved connection setting stops working.

entries.headline: Clearer meetings and a simpler Subscription window
features: The start screen names both kinds of meeting: a public open-floor meeting, or a private meeting you host.
Add a room password whichever way you start or join a meeting.
Hosts can show and copy their host password in the Host window.
Subscription has its own window in More, with each plan’s monthly and annual price side by side.
Focus shows everyone, camera on or off, and keeps faces in view.
Run app offers Take Turns and Whiteboard on any device.
fixes: Who’s here in Chat, Guestbook and games stays up to date.
Clearer labels and notes in Scroll view and on shared screens.

entries.headline: Faster joining and steadier captions
fixes: Joining a meeting across different networks is much faster.
Captions are steadier in every browser and restart on their own.
Smoother meetings on iPhone.

entries.headline: Simpler camera and mic choices
features: Phones open your front camera, with Flip in More to switch.
Clearer camera, mic and speaker pickers.
fixes: Smoother joining.

entries.headline: Captions on Android, and one-tap unmute
features: Live captions now work on Android phones, right on your device.
Tap Mic once to unmute. Pick a mic only when you have more than one.
fixes: If a mic can't be opened, your meeting goes back to the one that works.

entries.headline: Choose your mic, camera and speaker
features: Pick which microphone, camera or speaker your meeting uses.
A clear note tells you why your video stays soft and how to clear it.
Hide the agenda on your own screen.
Run app points you to the starter apps and the App Store.
fixes: Older versions you've opened keep loading offline, in every browser.
Connect Four seats always go to the right player.
Lighter blur choices.
Captions keep every line and mark the ones they're unsure of.

entries.headline: Smoother tipping
fixes: Paying in USDC now shows your tip in USDC, with a Back button.
Connect your wallet straight from the pay sheet.
Close payment notices with one tap. They stay closed.
A simpler meeting start form.

entries.headline: Easier tips
fixes: USDC tips on Base open your wallet right away, with tips up to $25 and a clearer message when a tip is over the limit.

entries.headline: Everyone, everywhere, by name
fixes: See everyone's name in the meeting, wherever they joined from.
USDC tips on Base open the wallet; tips up to $25; clearer over-limit message.
Meeting connector: more reliable meeting info for agents.

entries.headline: Smoother meetings on phones
fixes: Snappier phone controls, with tabs, tools and the view menu always ready.
New screen shares open right in front of you.
A cleaner top bar for host notices.
Smooth scrolling in full-screen meetings on Android.
Faster, quieter connections on restricted networks.
Meeting connector: built-in guidance for keeping passwords safe.

entries.headline: Steadier hosting and clearer tiles in meetings
fixes: The host's controls and presence now reach everyone, wherever they joined from.
Smoother admission when several people arrive at once.
When someone shares their screen, their tile now says "Presenting".
Clearer tiles when video is paused on a connection, showing the person's picture and one simple note.

entries.headline: Subscriptions for everyone in meetings
fixes: Subscriptions, passes and admin rooms are now available to everyone in meetings.

entries.headline: No Subscribe link in the App Store
fixes: The App Store no longer shows a Subscribe link. Subscriptions are for meetings: Subscribe stays in the meeting's More menu.

entries.headline: App Store: the Subscribe link keeps its name
fixes: The App Store's Subscribe link no longer shows as a second Home Screen button.

entries.headline: Subscribe from the meeting and the App Store
fixes: Meetings: More now has a Subscribe button. It opens the plans in Settings: $2 a month for admin rooms of up to 20 people, $5 a month unlimited, paid with PayPal.
Meetings: when video is paused on a connection, the message offers Subscribe and the 4-hour pass in every browser.
The App Store links to a new Subscribe page with the same plans.

entries.headline: Clearer Share and paused-video messages
fixes: Meetings: the Share sheet now fits the room and the reader. An open meeting says anyone with the link can join, and only the host is told the host password stays with them.
Meetings: when video is paused on a free link, the blur note no longer covers the paused-video message.

entries.headline: Chat floats over the meeting, a slimmer top bar, and steadier linked offices
fixes: Meetings: chat and the transcript open as a panel over the meeting instead of squeezing it, and on phones the top bar is one row with a … menu.
Meetings: when two offices are linked, call setup between people no longer travels over the link, and an office keeps exactly one backup link instead of two.
Meetings: on a free link between offices, the Stage is heard as part of the office's one sound stream, so it no longer turns to static.
Apps: the shared web proxy used by apps such as the Bible Browser now only serves GifOS pages that have joined properly.
Phones and laptops on battery: the low power level now starts at 27%.

entries.headline: Blurred faces say why, and Back keeps you in the meeting
fixes: Meetings: a blurred face now says why it is blurred, on its tile and on the Stage.
Meetings: blur is measured on the picture's long side, so it looks the same on every screen shape, and Min blur is stronger.
Android: the Back button no longer drops you out of a meeting. It opens More, where Float is one tap away. After you leave, Back works as usual.

entries.headline: A tidier meeting screen and steadier joins
fixes: Meetings: a join that was cut off when someone closed their connection is now sent again, so joins no longer stall.
Meetings: the Stadium no longer shows a count of people with no faces after someone leaves or drops out.
Meetings: the top bar, chat and floating bar now line up the same on every screen, and chat opens at the newest message.
Phones and laptops on battery: one power level (full, save, low) now sets how much video they send.

entries.headline: Joining works even when your device's clock is off
fixes: Meetings: a phone or computer whose clock runs a few minutes fast could not join, stuck at "Connecting to GifOS". It now joins normally.
Meetings: when a meeting needs a newer GifOS, the page now says to reload to update, instead of saying your internet may be down.
Android: a floating video from full screen now stays up when you switch to another app.
Android: returning to the meeting through the floating video's expand button no longer leaves a black tile behind.

entries.headline: Offices behind firewalls stay linked when someone leaves, and joining is steadier
fixes: Meetings: when the person linking two offices leaves, a spare link takes over in about two seconds, instead of the offices being cut off for half a minute.
Meetings: two offices linked through a relay switch to a direct connection when one appears, so the relay is used only while it is needed.
Meetings: on a network that is slow to look up names, the link between offices now uses the secure relay instead of a slower fallback.
Meetings: a newcomer is no longer kept waiting when a join request is lost as a connection closes.
Meetings: when two people claim the same seat, it is settled within seconds instead of both waiting.
Opening GifOS on a stalled network no longer leaves a blank page: it opens within a few seconds.
Open rooms: a second session of the same pass is the room's admin at once.

entries.headline: Meetings check that a real browser is joining
fixes: Meetings: before your browser joins, it does a quick check that proves it is a real visitor, usually in under a second. Automated floods can no longer pile into the meeting servers.
Meetings: if GifOS is ever very busy, the meeting screen says so and lets you in as soon as there is room, instead of saying your connection may be down.

entries.headline: A shared screen reaches everyone at once, and you always open the latest version
fixes: Meetings: when the room was locked while someone was still joining, their view of a shared screen could take up to a minute to start, or never start. It now starts within seconds.
Opening GifOS after an update now takes you to the new version at once, instead of the version you last used.
Safari: joining the same meeting again from the same tab no longer stops with "This page did not finish loading".
Meetings: the connection steps no longer say "your network blocks direct calls" when it is the other person's network that does.
GifOS Meet for iPhone now gets through firewalls that block direct calls, using the fallback relay; calls stay end-to-end encrypted.

entries.headline: Offices behind strict firewalls join one meeting, and healing is faster
features: Meetings: two offices or companies behind strict firewalls can now join the same meeting. A fallback relay links their rooms, passing only end-to-end encrypted media, and everyone sees, hears and counts everyone in the other rooms.
Meetings: if one end of a link between two offices drops out, a spare link takes over, so the far office keeps its sound.
Meetings: Follow the speaker now also follows people talking in other rows, zooming the Stadium to their tile.
Meetings: admin rooms can take a monthly or yearly plan through PayPal. A plan pays for video over the relay between offices, and several subscribers' shares add up for the whole meeting.
Payments: paid apps and the Creators tip jar can now be paid in USDC on Base.
Meetings: recording shows as a small REC badge on the floating bar.
Apps: one Save for every app, and a new page for making your own app for meetings.
Meetings: passes carry their own permissions, and several sessions of one pass can share one meeting.
Meet: Terms and Privacy links in Settings and next to every pay button. GifOS Meet has its own privacy page.
fixes: Meetings: the far office no longer sounds like static after a short loss on the link between offices.
Meetings: a newcomer is heard at once, instead of sometimes staying unheard for half a minute.
Meetings: someone who moves into your row hears you right away.
Meetings: a row that lost all its seats above it is reconnected in about a second instead of half a minute.
Meetings: a listener on the Stage could stay deaf after a connection change. They now keep hearing.
Meetings: a caption line spoken while people talk over each other is kept, not dropped.
Meetings: a newcomer who gets no answer at the door tries another way in only when the first one has really stalled, so joining is faster and steadier.
Meetings: the Stop sharing button on your own tile now stops the share.
notes: Known issue: once two networks joined by a relay can reach each other directly, the relay link stays open. Sound and video are fine; it only costs relay traffic.
Known issue: sound over the free relay is sent at 64 kbps; a lighter setting is planned.
Known issue: when one end of a link between two offices crashes, one far speaker can stay silent for about 6 seconds. Other far voices return within 2 seconds.
Known issue: someone watching from another row can wait a long time, tens of seconds, before a shared screen or a new Stage speaker shows up.
Known issue: a caption line one person's page keeps for another speaker is not yet shared with the whole room.

entries.headline: Voices in the Stadium and on the Stage keep their true pitch
fixes: Meetings: on a busy phone or computer, voices heard through the Stadium or the Stage could come out a little high, about a semitone and a half, for several seconds before drifting back. They now always play at their true pitch.

entries.headline: Everyone hears camera-off people, and sharing from the Row keeps your camera
fixes: Meetings: people in another row, a phone in a big room for example, could stop hearing someone whose camera was off, while their captions still arrived. Every voice now reaches every seat whatever the camera does.
Meetings: sharing a screen from the Row no longer freezes your Row tile or drops you from the Stadium. Your camera stays where it was; only stepping onto the Stage yourself takes it off the Row.

entries.headline: Joining works again with tracker blockers on
fixes: Meetings: people whose browser blocks trackers (tracking protection, iOS Safari's default privacy protection, or an ad blocker) could be stuck at "This page did not finish loading" and never reach the room. A blocked third-party script no longer stops a join.

entries.headline: Meetings rebuilt to grow without limit
features: Meetings are rebuilt from the ground up: a meeting can grow to any size, and it repairs itself when people drop out, freeze or come back.
Small meetings stay tightly connected, and the stage always has room for five speakers.
GifOS follows your browser's language, with a choice in Settings. English, Spanish, Russian, Simplified Chinese and German are included for the desktop, the store, meetings and the built-in apps.
Dates and times in meetings show in your language's format.
Reloading the page keeps your seat in a meeting: you come back to the same place instead of queueing as a newcomer.
The waiting room is for admin rooms only. In an open room there is no waiting-room button and nobody is held at the door; in an admin room the admin's Admit opens every door.
A new broadcast starts with neutral wording; the run-of-show is an optional host template.
Stadium video is much faster, and sound is clearer in big rooms.

Reactions now reach the whole meeting, like a raised hand, and there is a new ❤️ heart. In big rooms the Stadium shows who is talking (green), raised hands and reactions with colors, down to a single pixel per person.
Picture-in-picture: tap Float to keep the meeting in a small window, on Android and on desktop Chrome and Edge.

Joining is private: the screen before joining shows you with camera and mic off, and the camera does not turn on until you tap it. Turning the camera off really turns it off: the camera light goes out.

Captions are sent to the meeting by default, and you can turn that off in Settings. A new Transcript setting keeps a transcript for you or shares it with the room, with the language of each line. The "Transcribing" mark is now "Sending captions" and shows only when it is true. Whisper captions download their model once from gifos.app and your voice never leaves your device. A short notice tells you when captions are on in a meeting.

Settings in a meeting is a normal scrolling screen, popup buttons stay visible, the More menu is tidier, the bar never moves when the menu opens, and full screen fills a phone screen for camera faces.
Debug logging in Settings: turn it on, export the log, see its size and clear it.
fixes: In a meeting with an admin password, setting or changing the password sends everyone who does not have the new one back to the door to type it, so people who slipped in early are asked too.
Disruptive or broken pages have a harder time keeping newcomers out or creating duplicate people. A large group of disruptive pages can still keep newcomers out.
Vote-offs are counted inside the meeting.
When the admin changes the password, pages that do not hold the new one return to the door right away.
Chat after a reload is no longer lost, and a line said while you reconnect still reaches you.
Transcript lines merge correctly across languages: a person who switches language is written in the new one, and overlapping lines no longer double up.
A speaker on stage who reloads the page is back on stage faster.
Sound recovers more quickly when someone drops out.
A person who is still connected is no longer shown as gone, and someone coming back after a stall reconnects on the first try.
The Meeting Bot no longer starts twice.
notes: Update GifOS to the newest version: an older version still joins and talks, but until that page updates its Ban, Waiting room and vote-off buttons do nothing.
Spanish, Russian, Simplified Chinese and German strings are new. Please report any wording that reads wrong.
Known issue: right after someone leaves, the people count can read one too high for a moment before it settles.
Known issue: someone still on an older version can join and talk, but their Ban, Waiting room and vote-off buttons do nothing until their page updates.
Known issue: in very large rooms (about 1000 people) joining can be slow, and a large crowd of disruptive pages can still slow the room or keep newcomers out.
Known issue: when many people leave at once, the room can take a while to settle.
Known issue: in a Stadium, the picture of someone using Firefox is usually only slightly late, and occasionally up to about 0.3 seconds.
Known issue: memory use can grow slowly during a very long meeting; this is still being studied. A small computer running many meeting pages at once can run short of memory.
Known issue: a rare page crash in WebKit browsers, such as Safari, during a meeting is still being tracked down.
Known issue: automatic picture-in-picture on a computer when you switch tabs is not reliable yet. Tap Float before you switch.

entries.headline: Hotfix: no false "Still in the call", and a one-line app bar on phones
fixes: An app opened on its own (no meeting) no longer says "Still in the call" when you come back from another app. It shows only while you are in a meeting with your microphone or camera on.
On a phone, an app's top bar fits on one line again: GifOS, the app, Invite and a ⋯ menu with Save, Help, Abilities and Full screen.
Help and Abilities in an app's top bar open on the first tap again on a phone.
notes: Version numbers can now have a fourth part for quick fixes (0.9.24.1 comes after 0.9.24 and before 0.9.25).

entries.headline: Bigger meetings that stay in one piece
features: Meetings past one section: everyone seats, and each section has its own People list.
Transcripts label every line by the channel it was heard on: a person's name for a direct link, "Stadium" for the far rows.
Payments: the payment sheet offers PayPal only while USDC is switched off.
Tip GifOS Creators 1.1.
fixes: A new row-mate's camera no longer freezes on its tile after people move seats (rooms of any size).
The room count stays right after someone leaves, also with a deep seat and in rooms of exactly one full section.
A seat that went silent is dropped after about 90 seconds, so a frozen tile and a wrong count clear on their own.
A phone that was frozen or backgrounded rejoins in about two seconds when it wakes, even on a slowed clock.
Someone who leaves is no longer shown as gone from one page and still counted on another.
Joining a big meeting no longer stalls at the door.
With a hand up on a narrow window, the header keeps its count tap whole, and a short desktop window shows the count again.
A person in the waiting room no longer sees Invite.
notes: Known issue: in meetings of 26 or more, after someone rejoins or reloads into the first section, other people's lists can show them without a seat for up to about 30 seconds.
Known issue: after someone's device crashes, one person's header can read "Room count incomplete" for up to about a minute and a half before the count returns.
Known issue: if the link between two people in the first section drops for most of a minute, they can take up to about a minute to see each other again after it returns.
Known issue: a raised hand in a different section can take up to about 15 seconds to reach far seats.
Known issue: meetings of 80 people are new and not yet proven; some lists may stay incomplete after a big room fills.

entries.headline: Meetings hold together under stress
features: Captions: one person turning CC on can write down everyone in the meeting, including people on other rows.
Meeting transcript and recording downloads are named after the room.
fixes: A settled meeting no longer times out the mesh digest gate — the digest stays fast enough on a quiet machine.
When Deepgram closes, a Metadata frame that was already queued still fills the request id.
Renegotiation recovers when an answer never settles on a live pair, and a marked re-ask is scanned when its hand-off target goes dark.
Two offers on a link no longer cross; only the initiator sends the first offer, and a polite door asks before offering.
A muted stage voice stays muted — no relay rings for stage feeds.
A frozen video tile is detected and the link is rebuilt so the picture comes back while voice still plays.
A banned peer id stays dead until that device reloads as a new id.
Eagle Defense shows only START or PAUSE the moment the pad appears (apps-source).

entries.headline: Admins choose who can share a screen
features: In a meeting you run, Allow screen share on the meeting bar lets every guest share their screen. You can also allow or stop one person from their tile.
fixes: Guests in a meeting with an admin could not share their screen even when the admin wanted them to. The admin can now allow it directly.
Turning screen sharing off stops a share that is already going.

entries.headline: Broadcast opens again, and people who drop out of a meeting get back in fast
fixes: The Broadcast app on the Home Screen opens again. It used to reload itself over and over and never start.
If everyone in a small meeting lost their seat at once, nobody could get back in. The meeting now restarts itself.
Someone who reloaded while the meeting's host was offline could be left outside for good. They now get back in.
After someone's device froze and came back, the meeting could keep two hosts for minutes. It now settles in seconds.
Joining or rejoining while someone was offline could take 15 to 30 seconds. It now takes a few seconds.
A reloaded page goes straight back into the meeting it was in.
While you wait to get back in, the meeting no longer says "Just you"; it says it is getting you back in.

entries.headline: Meetings keep their picture on slow devices, and people who drop out come back fast
fixes: On a slow computer or phone, your blurred camera could stop sending for many seconds, so everyone saw your picture freeze. It now keeps sending.
Someone who lost their connection or went offline for a while now rejoins the meeting within seconds, even if the room rearranged while they were away.
Orca saves your grid again; it used to save an empty file.
Pixelit keeps a photo you opened after you close and reopen the file.
In Slots, a friend's spin now shows who pulled.
In Spider, choosing a new number of suits before a new game now deals that many suits.
In the JSON editor, Compact now works in Code mode.
In the LRC maker, the Stamp button keeps its own look.
A booted computer image no longer shows every folder twice.
Turning down the camera at the start of a meeting no longer leaves a hidden error behind.

entries.headline: Meetings recover cleanly, and your name shows from the start
features: When a newer GifOS release is out, the Home Screen, meetings and the sign page show one shared update bar.
A meeting link always opens the current release, so people on different versions still meet.
fixes: Your own tile now shows the name you choose, at the door or later in Settings. A fresh or private browser used to stay "Guest" on your own screen.

When someone in the front row lost their connection and came back, two people could claim the same seat and the room took minutes to sort it out. It now settles in seconds, even on a busy phone whose timers run slow.
Settings → Version no longer offers "Use latest" for a release it could not check while offline.
The screen-name prompt says what the name is for.

entries.headline: Meetings you can trust at any size
features: Offline Captions: a speech-to-text app that writes live captions on your own device, with no server. It installs in one tap and becomes the meeting's second captions engine.
Bible Study 0.9.0 joins the store, with all 139 translations and Listen.
An office, campus or phone carrier where many people share one internet address can now hold a meeting of any size. The relay no longer caps people per address.
Admin "Blur guests" and "Video off" now reach every guest in the room, including people who join later, not just the ones linked to the admin.
fixes: Security: a room member could forge messages that kicked another person out of their seat or kept a departed person's seat alive. Every such message is now proven to come from its real sender.
Everyone joins every meeting muted, camera off and fully blurred again. A build briefly remembered your last blur level between meetings.
Below the first 25 seats, people saw a shared screen but not the other presenters on Stage. Every seat now sees the same Stage.
A lost join request cost up to 30 seconds in a room with several greeters; now it costs a few seconds.
Big rooms heal and seat correctly after many people leave and rejoin at once; no more duplicate seats.
A presenter's phone no longer runs up to nine video encoders for backup copies nobody is watching.
Captions and goodbyes no longer flood the whole room, and a relay seat in a background tab keeps its video moving.
Dragging an icon on the Home Screen could be lost if the screen refreshed its badges mid-drag.

entries.headline: Meetings that scale: nothing a phone pays grows with the room
features: Big meetings: your phone now hears only its own section of up to 25 people. What the whole room needs — the count, raised hands, who is on Stage, votes, the shared app — arrives as a small summary folded up and down the tree. A room of a thousand costs each phone the same as a room of twenty.
Clear video needs everyone, at any size: one person staying blurred keeps the whole room blurred, and the room clears again when they agree.
Every room-wide message is signed by the person who sent it. Nobody can speak in someone else's name, and a phone passes on only what it has verified.
A flood guard: each phone takes only so many new messages a second from any one neighbour, and from any one sender. A misbehaving client can slow a meeting, never drown it.
Ban only works on a device the room's door vouched for, so a ban can never land on the wrong person.
Apps can pay you: tip jars and paid features through PayPal, a connected wallet, a wallet transfer or an AI agent, with the price signed by the app's author.
Yoinks joins the store.
fixes: A phone whose clock ran a minute slow was never counted as present, never allowed on Stage, and kept everyone who could hear it blurred. Presence is now judged by when a message arrived, not by the sender's clock.
One chat line, caption or file notice used to be re-broadcast by every phone that received it — a thousand floods for one line in a big room. Now the sender's is the only one.

Joining a busy room could put a newcomer's seat claim behind a ghost's, or reject a real one as stale, depending on how long each phone's page had been open. Seat claims now carry their age instead of a clock reading.
The relay sends newcomers only the room's greeters instead of the whole member list, so a large room can be joined at all; a burst of people joining at once no longer hits a cap.
A relay socket now has to stay open before its reconnect backoff resets, so a flapping connection no longer hammers the relay.
Ping Pong is no longer one of the default games: it never played well enough. Your other games and your own copies are untouched.

entries.headline: The Stage no longer freezes on a struggling computer, and the App Store opens at once
features: The App Store opens as fast as its catalog loads: it no longer reads every installed app off the disk (and hashes it) before drawing the first card. Which apps are yours, and which have an update, is read from the file index.
fixes: Meetings: when the person on Stage is on an overloaded computer their picture could freeze for everyone for 15–20 seconds at a time. Their encoder now sends a smaller picture while it is struggling instead of turning every frame into an expensive keyframe, and the keyframe nudge no longer flips the picture between sizes. Measured across four machines with the Stage computer deliberately overloaded: two freezes in six runs before, none in six after.
A pinned build that has been retired bounces you to the current one once and says so — unchanged, and exercised now that releases 0.9.0–0.9.11 are retired.
notes: Releases 0.9.0 through 0.9.11 are retired; the three most recent releases stay available to pin. Your files, apps and settings are untouched by any of this.

entries.headline: A security audit closed a critical sandbox hole — and forty-five new apps landed
features: Forty-five new app ports, including JupyterLite (a real Python notebook, offline), Monaco Code, SQL Playground, ffmpeg.wasm Studio, Webamp, Monkeytype, TIC-80, shapez.io, RegExr, SVG-Edit, Blockly Games, Learn Git Branching, Hydra, alphaTab, EPUB Reader, OpenJSCAD, CascadeStudio, DigitalJS, jsnes, Carbon, OTP Auth, Hanzi Writer, Trianglify, RAWGraphs, Background Removal, Smartcrop, Primitive, Matter Sandbox and Parable of the Polygons.

Bible study: export and import everything you have made as ONE stamped GIF, an Include Apocrypha toggle (off by default), and a study panel and search that dock beside the text on a wide screen instead of covering it.

Payments: receipts are bound to the claim that earned them and invoices to the payer, and there is now an agent rail (HTTP 402 with Stripe Shared Payment Tokens) for software that pays on your behalf.

Four apps — beepbox, Blockly Games, JupyterLite and SVG-Edit — no longer use the browser prompt() the sandbox answers with null, so their dialogs work: SVG-Edit’s five dialogs, beepbox’s clipboard fallback and Blockly’s variable prompt all ask properly now.
fixes: CRITICAL: a sandboxed app could navigate its own frame to any URL and keep its bridge to the desktop, with no CSP and no shim. The parent now pins frame-src to about:, an unload beacon freezes the bridge and re-mounts the app, and nested frames are swept (a srcdoc child had its own RTCPeerConnection). Every build before this one is affected, including pinned snapshots.
Meetings: names no longer cross the relay wire, a device tag is required to join, chat is bounded, and replayed joins are refused inside a fixed window.
Offline: the service worker now keys one cache entry per file, so an offline boot brings up the newest build this device actually ran instead of the one it was installed with.
notes: This release is a flag day for meetings: the derivation scheme is gifos-net-4, so clients from before and after it land in different relay sessions. The Workers must be deployed with it.
Link secrets are now 16 characters, room passwords are stretched with PBKDF2, signed orders carry monotonic timestamps, and an owned link’s verifier commits to the owner’s key.

entries.headline: Every game and tool on the Home Screen got a play-test on a phone — and a dozen new ports
features: New apps: Worldview (NASA satellite layers, a timeline, compare two days — with a Blue Marble that works offline), The House (a playable assembled house that makes sound), Sandspiel (a falling-sand world in the file), Bingo (a real hall — every phone speaks, fireworks on a verified win), plus Piano Trainer, Vintage Poker, fend, My Mind, JSON Editor, JSON Crack, Hexahedral, Blackjack, Server Survival and Backdooms as unofficial ports.

Over sixty existing apps were play-tested on a phone and fixed one by one: thumb pads and D-pads where a finger needs them, boards that fit the screen, empty states that say what to do, best scores and drafts kept in the file, and Invite that actually seats your friends (Ludo, Tanks, Aim, Coil, Crossword, Solitaire, Spider, Slots, Duck Hunt, Pac-Man, Queens, Memory, Tiny Yurts, Metronome, Tuner, QR, and more).
Share from a store card asks which link you mean: open the app in one tap, or the store listing. A ?run= link on a GitHub page opens the GIF — a blob link is rewritten to the raw file.
An app invite link is reused by default, so a day-old invite still works — and you can retire it and mint a fresh one. An empty app room explains itself instead of showing a blank page.
Opening an app is never a blank pane: the app's own animation and name show from the first second, the wait belongs to the app, and a light app fades in over the dark stage.
Help → About has a Report a problem link that pre-fills the GitHub issue with where you clicked it. Every page carries a static list of links for AI agents (llms.txt first).
The 0.8.x releases are retired. A computer still pinned to one is moved to the current release once, keeps everything, and is told why.
fixes: Turning Talk on in an app room showed a row of blank camera boxes under the app. The room is audio-only, so they are gone — the app keeps the whole screen.
The launch splash could swallow the first tap on a fast phone: the app was already running under it. It stops taking taps the moment the app appears.
A computer pinned to a retired build looped between the loader and a 404 forever, with its desktop unreachable. It now bounces home once.
Worldview: closing the layer browser left a blurred, unclickable map; the tablet bottom bar pushed its own controls off the screen; offline warnings had gone quiet.
The app-update popup's link was unreadable on some pages; the store card's action button sat in the wrong place.
Catch the Cat: two fingers zoom the board and one finger is still a tap.

entries.headline: The Home Screen games and tools are finished apps now — Ping Pong first
features: Ping Pong is table tennis: a real table, real paddles, spin you can see, first to 11. Slide to move — the paddle hits for you. Play the computer, or Invite a friend to the far end.
Chess can play the computer (Easy / Medium / Hard) on the device. Castling, en passant, and promotion work. Minesweeper has Easy through Expert, a first click that never dies, and flags.
Tic-Tac-Toe and Connect Four look like the real things, keep a series score, and Invite sits you in a seat.
Paint is a sketch pad with brush, fill, undo, and the picture saved in the icon. Notes is a notebook you can actually edit. The calculator traces a value when you point at a curve.
Stopwatch has hundredths and laps and keeps running if you close it. Chat and Guestbook empty rooms tell you to Invite. Fortune says so when it cannot reach the slip, instead of inventing one.
IRL party games: Fake Facts scores the real players, and Catch the Spy / The Dial / Odd Word Out work over Invite, not only pass-the-phone.
Help ends with Credits: who made the app, who brought it to GifOS, what it is based on, the license — sealed inside the signed app itself, so the credit travels with every copy.
App rooms can Talk: the host flips Talk on the app bar and everyone gets their own mic. Audio only for now — for video, start a meeting and run the app from there.
The App Store installs, updates, and opens from the card — one button that says what you can do next — and a Works offline pill marks apps that never touch the network.
fixes: Ping Pong used to be a brown gym with dots for paddles and a ball you had to tap. It now rallies.
Fake Facts (and Same Brain) printed “? fooled: ?” and never scored — they were reading the player id wrong.
Catch the Spy, The Dial, and Odd Word Out were private to one phone, so an Invite never synced.
Tilt could not use the accelerometer inside the app frame.
An app room had no way to start a call at all: everything was there, nothing opened the door.
The update bar's link was unreadable on dark app pages.

entries.headline: Civiclock, a bigger IsoCity, and an app can’t bounce you into a meeting
features: Civiclock is in the store: a small city that ticks — homes, shops, power, water, people, night lights, blackouts. Invite a co-mayor.
IsoCity is now 16×16. Pinch or Ctrl+scroll to zoom, undo the last stroke, and New city asks before wiping the map.
Deepgram speech-to-text talks to Deepgram directly. Your key and your audio never pass through our proxy.
An app can ship its own Help page inside the GIF; the Help button shows it. Every Help screen also explains Invite, Save, Steal and remixing.
fixes: Tapping an ordinary link inside an app no longer dumps you into the meeting lobby. This is the reason for the release — 0.9.10 still did it.

entries.headline: A Camera that saves, a My Media that edits, and a vocal remover that runs on your own machine
features: Vocal Remover is in the store: splits a song into vocals and everything else, on your device, nothing uploaded. It is slow without a graphics chip — expect most of an hour for a four-minute song. There is a Stop button and a “first 30 seconds” preview.
Big model files download when you first press Separate, not at install.
Camera on the Home Screen: live preview, filters, Burst, Boomerang and time-lapse. Only offers what your device can actually do.
My Media: download a file, turn a video clip into a looping GIF, flip photos and videos, clip or reverse recordings. Edits are new items; the original stays.
My Media: select several items to file or delete. Delete goes to Deleted first; a second Delete removes for good.
Ports of other people’s apps are credited to their authors and marked unofficial (Vocal Remover, FPS Simple).
You can tip an app or pay to feature a listing — no account needed. Install stays free.
Any app GIF can be handed to an AI and changed — ask for dark mode or bigger buttons, drop the new GIF on your Home Screen.
fixes: Camera photos on computers were saving as a black square. Fixed — the photo is now taken from the preview you see.
Camera saves every shot the moment you take it, including a video you stop by closing the viewfinder. Before, only the last shot survived and closing right after a recording lost it.
Camera has a My Media button, and the flip button that did nothing is gone.
Vocal Remover finishes on a phone: a 12 MB upload that froze the app is fixed, and a fake software “graphics chip” is refused rather than hung on.
Opening an app that still needs a big download shows the download progress instead of a blank pane.

entries.headline: Screen sharing in meetings, and FPS Simple works on a phone
features: Share your screen in a meeting. Pick a window or a display; it goes out like your camera does, and there is a clear Stop.
A room with an app pinned doesn’t offer screen sharing — the app already runs on everyone’s device, which is sharper. The Share sheet offers Run app first.
FPS Simple: a Watch demo button that plays on its own, full screen, in a loop.
FPS Simple: the map now shows where shots come from.
fixes: Inviting someone from a solo app left the room with no meeting bar or grid. Fixed.
The chat panel covered half the toolbar, so Record, CC, Stage, Settings and Help couldn’t be clicked while chat was open. Fixed.
Picking an app in a meeting no longer ends the meeting — the picker used to list Broadcast and the App Store, which navigate away.
FPS Simple: the bottom half of the screen was fogged over and the gun showed as a black silhouette. Fixed.
FPS Simple: the sky was black on some phones. Fixed.
FPS Simple: sound stopped cutting out during firefights.
FPS Simple: aiming works on touchscreen laptops, and the left thumbstick works in every direction.
FPS Simple: Play responds immediately and shows loading progress instead of a black screen.
Playing a game no longer counts as idle, so your phone doesn’t dim mid-game.
A shared app no longer restarts for everyone when one device gets busy, and no longer goes silent for one person while everything looks connected.
The App Store no longer offers an app your build can’t run (the check was skipped on the edge build).
Anyroad: rivers no longer hang in the air above their valley.

entries.headline: A faster Home Screen, PDF tables to spreadsheets, and an offline voice
features: The Home Screen appears right away — icons no longer wait for every app to be read first. Measured: 4.7 s to first icon before, a third of a second after.
PDF Tables turns a PDF’s tables into an Excel file. PDF Tables OCR does the same for scanned PDFs, using your graphics chip. Nothing is uploaded.
An offline neural text-to-speech voice that runs on your graphics chip. Pick it in Settings.
Apps can ask for the graphics chip; you approve it like any other permission.
The App Store has a Share button that copies a clean link to an app.
fixes: Anyroad no longer slows to a crawl on a long drive — memory is released as you travel.
Anyroad: rivers and lakes draw where they are, bridges are driven across and tunnels through, street names stop being erased by the sky.
Chess pieces no longer flicker while you drag them.

entries.headline: Links that open an app already doing something, and a chat that keeps every conversation
features: A link can open an app with the first move made — e.g. Anyroad already flying over the Grand Canyon. You see what the link asks for and say yes first. Anyroad’s ☰ sheet copies a link to where you are.
Host an app GIF anywhere and share the link — no store submission needed. Now documented properly.
Ask AI keeps every chat, with a History list and a search that reads whole conversations. Only the trash button deletes.
AI answers arrive word by word, including from models on your own device.
A second offline voice, KittenTTS Nano: eight voices, 24 MB download. The 1.6 MB eSpeak voice stays.
When you join someone’s app you see a progress bar while it copies over.
fixes: The offline text models warn you they are slow before you install them, not after.
A staged speaker’s video no longer freezes for people watching through someone else.
Sound It Out: the sight-word list is shared with everyone in the room, so both screens agree.

entries.headline: Video that recovers in a second, provider apps, and Sound It Out
features: Provider apps: put one in the Providers folder, give it a job in Settings → AI models, and every app that needs that job uses it. Four to start: offline text-to-speech and three small text models (BitNet, Gemma 3, Gemma 4). All run on your device.
Big model files download separately, are checked, stored once, and removed with the app. They stay out of backups.
Anyroad: fly. Press the aeroplane and the car takes off. Races put a flag on a real road for everyone.
Anyroad: you start stopped and press GO. Street names, a flare to be found by, thicker woods, a speedometer and altimeter, damage that still drives home, and shooting at friends.
Calculator draws graphs as you type: curves, polar, implicit, inequalities, sliders for variables.
Sound It Out is in the store: any word or sentence sounded out letter by letter in your own recorded voice. Also sight words.
The store shows the oldest GifOS each app needs, on the card.
Stealing an app asks whether you want the data too, and works offline.
The recording indicator can be dragged and remembers where you put it.
fixes: When someone’s connection dropped, everyone downstream froze for six seconds and sometimes never recovered. Now the room routes around them in about a second.
A staged speaker with camera off no longer vanishes for listeners after twenty seconds.
A one-tap app link sent to a first-time visitor used to land on an empty Home Screen. It carries now.
Stealing an app shows its progress on the button you pressed.
Recording audio no longer dims the page.
The App Store grid now says when an app has an update.

entries.headline: Rooms that split, a voice that went missing, a door that jammed
fixes: Two people in the same room couldn’t see or hear each other if a browser had saved a password for a different room. GifOS now checks the room’s password and forgets a wrong one.
On stage with your camera off, the room stopped hearing you after twenty seconds. Fixed.
A room could get stuck so nobody new could join. Fixed.
Opening your own app no longer flashes the meeting toolbar first.
Someone who leaves is properly forgotten instead of lingering in the list for a minute.
Offline, a link to a saved version opens that version, not the newest.

entries.headline: Older phones and computers can join meetings again
features: Meetings work on much older browsers. GifOS carries its own copy of the signature code when the browser lacks it; security is unchanged.
Plain-language explanations when a browser genuinely can’t do something.
fixes: Opening your own app no longer shows the “browser too old” message — that check only matters when you share it live.
The badge on built-in apps is smaller and quieter.

entries.headline: Old browsers get a straight answer, big rooms seat reliably
features: A browser that’s too old for meetings is told exactly which version it needs. A new Browsers page (from About) lists what works.
Firefox is in the test fleet.
fixes: Large rooms could hand the same seat to two people, or jam partway through a mass join. Fixed.
A seat reserved for someone still joining can no longer be stolen by a stale goodbye.

entries.headline: Joining works again — the demo-night failure, fixed
features: Meeting and Broadcast keep separate Recent & saved lists.
Plainer wording for connection errors, passwords, blur and the privacy explainer.
fixes: Joining no longer waits on the camera prompt. You get your seat at once and the camera joins when you allow it.
One person’s bad link can’t knock someone else out of their seat; a dropped phone rejoins in seconds.
Share links from the newest build open on phones that have never visited before.
A broadcast link reopens as a broadcast.

entries.headline: Three meeting bugs that hid behind flaky tests
fixes: Stopping a shared app sticks for everyone, even if people join or leave at that moment.
Video frozen after a split room rejoins now recovers on its own.
Joining during a connection blip no longer wedges your seat.

entries.headline: Apps and meetings became one thing — and an App Store
features: Everyone needs this build to meet: rooms are addressed differently, so 0.8.8 or older lands in a different room.
An App Store on your Home Screen. The app downloads once, on Install.
Every app is a room: one link and someone joins you inside it, with video.
An app opened alone gets the whole window.
Share your screen into a room.
Home Screen icons are locked until you choose Arrange.
fixes: Scrolling a phone no longer drops apps into folders.
The camera stops flipping sideways and keeps its real shape.
If the person hosting an app leaves, the room freezes and hands over instead of losing your work.

entries.headline: Longer phone battery in big meetings
features: Two lighter video sizes (down to 144p) for phones low on battery.
An all-muted room wakes far less often.

entries.headline: Deeper phone power savings
features: Phones run video one to two sizes lighter in every state.

entries.headline: Build badge on every page
features: A small corner badge shows which build you’re running.
fixes: Restored the version-pinning safeguard a loader redesign had broken.

entries.headline: Invite links and room names fixed
fixes: Invite links (/meet, /call, /join) open the meeting again instead of the Home Screen.
Room names keep their capital letters, so the same link lands everyone in the same room.
Sharing an app into a meeting works for guests again.
The build number in the Version panel counts correctly.

entries.headline: Fullscreen view and a smoother join
features: Fullscreen view: one feed big, the rest as floating thumbs.
Joining shows a veil until your seat is real.
Video quality eases down to match your battery.

entries.headline: Honest video, camera flip, fullscreen, votes
features: Tiles show your whole camera frame, not a cropped square.
Flip between front and back cameras.
A real fullscreen button.
Recordings carry a burned-in “Recording — name” badge.
Vote someone onto the stage, off it, or out of the room.

entries.headline: A relay blip can’t split a room
features: Diagnostics show when someone’s media arrives via a friend.
fixes: A relay hiccup no longer strands joiners or spawns a duplicate room.

entries.headline: First public release
features: Every app is a real animated GIF you own — drop it on your Home Screen and it runs. Share the file, share the app with its data inside.
Peer-to-peer meetings with no server in the middle; run any app live inside one.
Any app goes multiplayer with one invite link.
Works fully offline; back up a whole computer as one GIF.
Ten themed computers, signed apps, and per-person AI/API keys that apps use but never see.
